overall: The AG found a violation for an executive session notice that omitted the bargaining units named at the meeting, but no violation on the minutes-review claim. The Committee was ordered to comply and was credited for already fixing the notice.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the January 30 executive session notice (contract negotiations and collective bargaining) did not identify the bargaining units involved.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we conclude that the topic as listed on the January 30 notice should have included these bargaining units and failure to do so was a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Committee failed to periodically review executive session minutes to determine whether a continued purpose for nondisclosure existed.
allegations.key_passage: Absent evidence to the contrary, we credit the public body’s statement and find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law in this regard.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
